title: QueueLeaseBlock
description: A candidate intentionally not leased by the v2 scheduler.

conflicts_with.description: Existing execution that caused the conflict, when applicable.

ExecutionFence.description: Complete ownership envelope for one workflow execution generation.

queue_lease.description: Queue lease CAS identity. Direct execution may omit it.

repository.description:
Repository/ref reservation. Non-code workflows may omit it; coding
schedulers must require it before workspace preparation.

subject.description: Subject generation, absent only for a genuinely subjectless workflow.

workflow_generation.description:
Positive workflow generation. Reattachment keeps it; an intentional new
execution generation must increment it.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow id. Recovery preserves this id.

QueueLeaseBlockReason.description: Why a v2 lease candidate was left untouched.

oneOf.description: The exact subject generation already has an active execution.
Another active execution owns the repository/head ref.

The entry has an expired assignment that must be reconciled/recovered,
never handed out as fresh work.
The stored entry lacks the identity needed for fail-closed scheduling.

QueueLeaseFence.description: Compare-and-swap identity for the queue lease currently owning a workflow.

expires_at.description:
Backend-clock expiry. Expiry makes the lease recoverable, never an
ordinary fresh-leasing candidate.

generation.description:
Positive monotonic lease generation. Recovery transfers ownership by
incrementing this value, fencing the previous daemon instance.

owner_id.description:
Daemon/scheduler instance currently authorized to renew or terminalize
the lease.

RepositoryReservation.description: Repository/ref ownership reserved for one execution generation.

head_ref.description:
Fully-qualified mutable head ref owned by this run, for example
`refs/heads/animus/TASK-1175`.

repository.description:
Canonical repository identity. Hosts SHOULD use a normalized remote URL
or provider `owner/name` identity and compare it case-insensitively where
the provider does.

SubjectGeneration.description: A canonical subject identity and the immutable generation being executed.

generation.description:
Positive backend/queue generation. A later generation cannot be
satisfied by work or proof from an earlier one.
